item.title: Georgia Bulldogs pull off shocking recruiting flip, land five-star prospect over Texas A&M and Miami
item.description: Mark Matthews, a five-star offensive tackle, stunned the recruiting world by flipping from Texas A&M to Georgia instead of the expected Miami flip.
item.content:encoded:
With how insane this year has been in college football, it can be easy to forget there’s an entirely separate season unfolding off the field.

If you're a college football sicko, you know exactly what I'm referring to: recruiting.

Talent acquisition is a 24/7/365 business, and this latest recruiting cycle is reaching its climactic end, with early signing day a little less than a month from today.

ED ORGERON-LANE KIFFIN PAIRING ALREADY PAYING DIVIDENDS FOR LSU TIGERS DURING PIVOTAL RECRUITING WEEKEND

With that in mind, many of the nation's top prospects are already committed to their future schools, but that hasn't stopped some fireworks from occurring on the recruiting front these past few months.

Everyone thought the Florida Gators had pulled off the shocker of the season when they flipped five-star Texas commit and Louisiana native Easton Royal while also keeping him away from Lane Kiffin and the in-state LSU Tigers.

Georgia saw their rivals pull off a recruiting coup and said, "Hold my sweet tea," as they snatched another five-star recruit committed to a different school from the Lone Star State.

Here's the craziest part: they did it under cover of darkness while keeping him out of the clutches of a surging school right down the road.

Meet Mark Matthews, a five-star offensive tackle from South Florida powerhouse high school St. Thomas Aquinas.

If his name sounds familiar, it's because I wrote about him back in May when he originally committed to the Texas A&M Aggies and did so in relatively cringeworthy fashion, but that's beside the point.

As the losses continued to pile up this season for TAMU, so too did the decommitments, and their latest loss was the cornerstone to their offensive line haul in the 2027 class.

With his proximity to Miami-Dade County coupled with the fact that Mario Cristobal and offensive line coach Alex Mirobal have pretty much gotten whoever they've wanted in the trenches out of high school, it felt like a foregone conclusion that Matthews would end up flipping to the Hurricanes.

SOMEHOW, THE MIAMI HURRICANES HAVE DONE IT AGAIN WITH YET ANOTHER HEISMAN-LEVEL QUARTERBACK

So much so, that recruiting expert Steve Wiltfong logged a prediction for Matthews to end up in orange and green come signing day.

Guys like Wiltfong rarely get these types of things wrong, as all signs pointed to the Canes adding another five-star to their already historic recruiting class.

Then came the shocker.

How does Kirby Smart do it?

This felt like the most obvious Miami flip in recent recruiting history, yet Kirby was somehow able to waltz into Cristobal's backyard and take a five-star prospect at a position that the Canes head coach specializes in developing.

As far as recruiting coups go, this one was a shocker.

Experts are still trying to figure out how the Dawgs were able to pull this one off, but this should be a lesson to never count Kirby out of any recruiting race.

He's as relentless as anyone on the trail, dating back to his time as Nick Saban's defensive coordinator and right-hand man at Alabama.

Just like a tiger stalking his prey, even if you can't see him, it doesn't mean he isn't there lurking.

Go against Kirby on the recruiting trail at your own risk; you've been warned.

item.title: NFC-leading 49ers continue to push chips in and acquire star wide receiver Keenan Allen from Colts
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen before the deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The NFC-leading San Francisco 49ers are making moves at the trade deadline.

The 49ers acquired Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen for a 2027 sixth-round pick, the teams announced on Tuesday. The six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver will provide a major boost to the 49ers' receiving corps, which has been decimated by injuries.

Mike Evans has missed the last two games with Achilles and rib injuries, Deebo Samuel has missed the last three games with a hamstring injury, Christian Kirk is on injured reserve with a meniscus injury, second-round rookie De’Zhaun Stribling is on injured reserve with an ankle injury but hopes to return in December, and Ricky Pearsall is out for the season with a PCL injury.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Despite all those injuries, the 49ers are 7-1 and atop the conference. Allen has been productive in eight games with the Colts this season, catching 40 passes for 351 yards and a touchdown.

Allen was arrested in August on charges of two misdemeanor OWI (operating while intoxicated) offenses. He has not been disciplined because the legal process is still ongoing. He could face a three-game suspension once that process is concluded, as that is the typical suspension length under the NFL’s personal conduct policy.

Allen is in his 14th season in the NFL. He spent the first 11 seasons of his career with the Chargers franchise, including four seasons in San Diego before the team relocated to Los Angeles, before being traded to the Chicago Bears. He spent one season with the Bears before re-signing with the Chargers last year.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In August 2026, he signed with the Colts during training camp. Over his career, he has caught 1,095 passes for 12,402 yards and 71 touchdowns.

The Allen trade is the second transaction the teams have completed together this season. In October, the 49ers acquired All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner for a 2027 fourth-round pick.

For the Colts, the Allen trade is the third trade they have made since firing general manager Chris Ballard. They also traded eight-time Pro Bowl selection Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks.

The Colts may not be done, either, as running back Jonathan Taylor has drawn interest and wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade after the team parted with Nelson and Buckner.

The trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Thursday.

item.title: Pat McAfee comes to Josh Allen's rescue, Dianna Russini's new show gets roasted & DOGS!
item.description: Pat McAfee repeatedly warned Josh Allen they were live on television before he could speak, saving him from a potential hot mic moment on the show.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Folks, I am counting my lucky stars over here.

Over the weekend, my husband was pulling his work trailer out of our garage when — unbeknownst to him — the garage door got hooked on a 32-foot ladder tied to the top of the trailer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

You can probably already guess how this ends. The frame was busted, and the whole garage door was ripped off its tracks and bent all to hell. Disaster.

Of course, home ownership is a constant string of unexpected expenses, but we thought for sure this was going to be a few-thousand-dollar mistake. Not great anytime but especially not great two months before our Costa Rica trip.

We braced our wallets for impact.

But in a remarkable stroke of good fortunate, a technician came out this morning, saved the garage door, put it all back together again and added a new seal ... for $175! Consider my flabbers gasted. I thought I was being punked.

Anyway, this isn't an ad for an overhead door company. But it is an explanation for why I'm in one heck of a good mood today. I feel like I just hit the lottery.

So crack yourself a celebratory beer on my behalf, and let's get to some Nightcaps.

Man, what an absolute snoozer of a Monday Night Football game that was. Carson Wentz... woof.

You know, in past years, it would make me absolutely sick to see the Bills dominate like that. As a Dolphins fan, I mean. But this year? The tank is on, and my stress is gone.

It's such a freeing feeling to have zero expectations whatsoever.

Besides, at least Josh Allen is likable. So likable, in fact, that the families of opposing players are cheering for him and hounding him for photos.

After last night's game, the son of Vikings' long snapper Andrew DePaola took off his dad's jersey to reveal a Bills shirt underneath.

Unbelievable stuff. If you're DePaola can you even be mad, though? I mean, he's a former MVP and, well, you're a long snapper.

No offense to long snappers, of course.

The kid is one thing. But when DePaola's WIFE chased Josh down for a selfie... yikes.

Now I'm not a WAG, so I don't know the etiquette. But is it standard for players' wives and girlfriends to be out there fan-girling? To me, it feels very — I don't know — unprofessional? Sort of like media members taking selfies with players or asking for autographs — which does happen sometimes, but it is taboo.

Anyway, while we're on the topic of Josh Allen, how about Pat McAfee absolutely saving his butt during the pregame show?

In case it wasn't immediately apparent, Josh approaches McAfee during a live hit, and before Josh can say anything, McAfee lets him know over and over they are live on television.

This is akin to warning your buddy he's on speakerphone or that you're talking to him through the Bluetooth in your car.

Of course, that's not to assume Josh was going to say anything offensive or vulgar. Maybe he was going in with a simple, "Good evening, gentlemen, lovely weather we're having!"

But more than likely McAfee was anticipating something a little more colorful. So good on him for saving his friend from the hot mic.

The internet has enough to be fake outraged about without Josh Allen dropping an F-bomb or a d-ck joke or something.

Look, we knew Dianna Russini would eventually land on her feet after that whole Mike Vrabel scandal. It was just a matter of which outlet was going to be brave enough to hire her.

Enter BetUS. Whatever the heck that is. I guess one of the 472 options for online sportsbooks we have these days.

She's getting a show called "The Russini Report," which debuts tomorrow. And I've got to be honest with you guys — the production value could be better.

Apparently, I'm not the only one who thinks so.

I know Bobby Burack wrote a whole column on this yesterday, but the way in which this woman is just blatantly rejecting all accountability for her role in the affair is mind blowing.

PEOPLE did an interview with her, and during the interview, she repeatedly played the victim card. And at one point, she said she hoped her resiliency could be an inspiration to other women.

I think Dustin here says it best.

We can make fun all we want, by the way, but the fact is this show is going to do NUMBERS. At least the first few episodes will. Because we'll all tune in out of sheer morbid curiosity.

But hey, whatever cashes those checks, I guess.

Let's open the mailbag.

🐦 Twitter/X: @TheAmberHarding

📸 Instagram: @amberharding

While all of you were watching election returns last Tuesday, my husband, our dog and I were tucked away in a cozy nature retreat in Sparta, Tennessee — avoiding all forms of email, work and depressing news coverage.

Just a little slice of paradise.

It even had one of those Japanese toilets! IYKYK.

The hiking was a little rainy, but the fall colors were on point.

And since you guys always like to know what Rocky is up to, here's him living his best life at Scott's Gulf Wilderness State Park.

Now let's check in with the dogs y'all sent me this week.

And each issue has a Good Dog story. I’m going to go out on a limb and guess your favorite will be the Reader’s Choice runner-up.

item.title: F1 Great Riccardo Patrese explains why he told Kimi Antonelli he had to win a championship this season
item.description: Riccardo Patrese reveals the preseason advice he gave Kimi Antonelli before the young Mercedes F1 driver ended Italy's 70-year title drought.
item.content:encoded:
Mercedes F1 driver Kimi Antonelli became the first Italian driver to claim a World Drivers' Championship since the legendary Alberto Ascari won his second in 1953.

It was an incredible run that, it turns out, started with some wisdom from another Italian F1 great, Riccardo Patrese.

Patrese competed in F1 from 1977 to 1993, driving for numerous teams like Benetton and Williams, and won six Grand Prix, including the 1982 Monaco Grand Prix while with Brabham.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Kimi is a very good friend of my family, and we are friends of Kimi's family as well. So we’ve known each other very well for a long time," Patrese told OutKick over Zoom, promoting Jackpot City Casino. "So in the end, to see Kimi be world champion is a fantastic feeling because, for me, it's like [having] another son."

That relationship, coupled with his own 256 Grand Prix starts, made Patrese a perfect person to offer some advice to the young Italian.

Advice which centered on the fact that Mercedes came into the year with the best car on the grid.

"I said to him, ‘Look, Kimi, you have to be really world champion this year because it's an important [year],’" Patrese recalled. "Because at the beginning of the season, Mercedes was the best car, the strongest car, and of course ... you never know if next year it can be the same."

Antonelli at least seemed to have taken that to heart because he made the most of Mercedes' early dominance, including a run of five straight wins through the spring.

That gave the 20-year-old enough of a points cushion when other teams started to catch up in the development race as the season progressed, and he clinched the title earlier this month in Mexico City.

It's a historic win given Antonelli's age, but also because of what it means for Italian motorsport.

Before Antonelli's title, the closest any Italian driver had come was P2, and that was Patrese himself in 1992.

Patrese said that Antonelli's win is already inspiring the next wave of Italian drivers.

"We have other young talented drivers in Italy, but now that Kimi is world champion, it automatically [gives] enthusiasm, and motorsport in Italy is growing. It also happened with [Jannik] Sinner, a tennis player, [when he] became number one. Now everybody wants to play tennis, and let's hope that now everyone wants to be a racing driver."

item.title: Senate GOP rebellion fizzles as Thune keeps power despite historic midterm massacre
item.description: John Thune secured another term as Senate GOP leader despite Ron Johnson and Rick Scott pushing to delay elections after midterm losses.
item.content:encoded:
There was neither an exodus nor a mass housecleaning in the Senate GOP leadership, despite frustration and rumblings of discontent among some lawmakers reeling from last week’s devastating midterm losses.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., secured another term as the top Republican behind the closed doors of the Old Senate Chamber, where lawmakers charted their course for their few remaining weeks in power and beyond.

Thune, along with the bulk of his leadership team, which now includes Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, were swiftly elected after a group of Republicans failed to delay the leadership elections. 

It wasn't without a fight, though, with conversations behind closed doors dragging on for over seven hours. 

GOP SENATOR WITHHOLDS SUPPORT FOR THUNE AS LEADERSHIP SHOWDOWN LOOMS

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., led the charge to delay, and didn't stick around after his attempts to do so failed on a 31 to 15 vote in the Old Senate Chamber to proceed with the scheduled election. 

Johnson and others wanted to have a deep conversation about what had happened during the midterm elections, and a roadmap on what Republican leadership candidates could accomplish with the little time they had left in power. 

SENATE GOP REBELS MOVE TO DELAY LEADERSHIP VOTE, DEMAND RECKONING AFTER MIDTERM DISASTER

But there was no opposition to any of the lawmakers running for leadership. 

"This has never been anything against John Thune," Johnson said. "I think he has been very unfairly attacked, you know, by our base, and I don't agree with that. What I didn't agree with was holding the election right away, giving nobody an opportunity to really challenge any leadership position."

On Monday, Thune was adamant that he’d still run but was unsure of the outcome.

"That's the hope," Thune said when asked if he had the Senate GOP’s support. "You never know right until they vote."

Before the vote, Johnson and a handful of others believed there should be a shakeup in leadership, but didn’t offer an alternative to Thune.

"After the stunning defeat, you just can't continue on business as usual," Johnson said. "I mean, that kind of defeat demands change."

When asked if he’d be interested in running, Johnson said, "That’s part of the problem. Would you want it?"

"I think there's a number of people with talent," Johnson said. "Again, I'm not — at a minimum, we need to see out of our leadership team what's the strategy moving forward, and you can't come off of a defeat like that and just ram through elections and oh yeah, ‘let's just elect that leadership team by acclamation.’"

Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., had previously run for leader twice and most recently against Thune. But the lawmaker, who joined Johnson’s crusade for change, declined to throw his hat into the arena again.

"I think we have to acknowledge the voters are not happy," Scott said. "We have to start listening to voters."

CONGRESS RETURNS TO BRUTAL LAME-DUCK STRETCH WITH SHUTDOWN DEADLINE, LEADERSHIP RACES: 'CLOSET IS FULL OF S—'

Scott wanted ironclad promises on the GOP’s to-do list, including ramming through judicial nominees, government funding "without a massive omnibus," a stock trade ban, permitting reform, passing the National Defense Authorization Act, taking another crack at the SAVE America Act and balancing the budget — possibly through budget reconciliation.

Johnson and Scott were joined by Sens. Ted Budd, R-N.C., Mike Lee, R-Utah, John Kennedy, R-La., Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Dave McCormick, R-Pa., in a push to delay the elections that was not met, and the would-be coup faded as the secret ballots were cast.

Still, there were others outside that cohort who weren’t happy with last week and believed that there should be deeper soul-searching on what Republicans did over the last two years that led to a historic night for Senate Democrats.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., contended that much of what the GOP listed as accomplishments over their time in power is what worked against them.

"And, you know, you have the kind of record that this Congress has had, I think we better have a pretty tough family conversation about what it is we're doing," Hawley said.

"When you cut Medicaid, but you fund data centers, when you cut rural hospital funding, but you fund Planned Parenthood, when you let the cost of healthcare for working people go through the roof, but you can't do anything for them on other issues of affordability, from fertilizer to gas," he continued. "Yeah you know what? The public doesn’t like that very much."

item.title: Rory McIlroy shares scathing thoughts on Bryson DeChambeau and his future in competitive golf
item.description: Rory McIlroy took a pointed shot at Bryson DeChambeau's limited options ahead of the DP World Tour Championship, saying he'd never want to be in his shoes.
item.content:encoded:
Rory McIlroy has not tried to hide the fact that he is not particularly fond of Bryson DeChambeau, and actually used those exact words while talking about the two-time major winner during The Open held this past July. While that may make McIlroy's most recent comments about DeChambeau and his future completely predictable, it doesn't mean they are not noteworthy.

Speaking ahead of this week's DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, McIlroy was asked about DeChambeau potentially joining the European circuit.

DeChambeau's only option to play competitive golf in 2027 would be to join the DP World Tour with LIV Golf shutting down. At this moment in time, there is no immediate pathway back for DeChambeau to join the PGA Tour for next season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

While McIlroy accurately admitted that DeChambeau playing on the DP World Tour would bring more exposure to the circuit all around, he didn't end his thought without taking a shot at the American.

"Yeah, look, I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad -- he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy explained on Tuesday in Dubai.

"And honestly, look, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn't seem like he's got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

McIlroy is stating what the entire golf world already knew with his comment about never wanting to be in DeChambeau's shoes, but there is a difference between the golf world assuming it and McIlroy actually saying it while sitting inside of a media center. It adds a certain gravitas to the situation, and the rivalry that has built up between the two over recent years.

McIlroy and DeChambeau have a history with one another that has largely unfolded on golf's biggest stages, with the main highlights being DeChambeau getting the best of McIlroy at the 2024 U.S. Open and McIlroy returning the favor at the 2025 Masters by sliding on the green jacket for the first time.

Players have until Nov. 16 to commit to competing on the DP World Tour for next season, and whether or not DeChambeau elects to do so is a guessing game at this point.

DeChambeau issued a statement regarding LIV Golf closing its doors, but did not make mention of what his competitive golf future will entail.

The 33-year-old is exempt into all four major championships through 2029 thanks to his victory at the 2024 U.S. Open, which presents a possibility that he could turn even more of his focus to growing his YouTube channel and only competing in the majors.

item.title: Democrats accused of 'No Kings' hypocrisy over push to change voter-approved trans sports measures
item.description: Colorado's Philip Weiser and Rep. Pramila Jayapal face "No Kings" hypocrisy claims after signaling efforts to overturn transgender sports ballot measures.
item.content:encoded:
Voters in two Democratic strongholds approved restrictions on transgender participation in girls' sports last week, delivering rare Republican victories amid a blue wave. But Democratic officials are already discussing ways to change the measures, drawing accusations of hypocrisy from Republicans who point to their support for the "No Kings" movement.

Colorado Gov.-elect Philip Weiser, who also criticized a separate ballot measure restricting gender-related surgeries for minors, and Rep. Pramila Jayapal , D-Wash., both raised objections to the measures approved in their respective states.

At his first post-election news conference, he suggested Colorado's Democratic-controlled legislature could revisit the voter-approved measures, saying that it is "statutory … and a natural and I believe appropriate role for the legislature to say ‘what are the adjustments that need to be added."

PRO-TRANS ACTIVISTS HOLD RALLY AGAINST WASHINGTON STATE BALLOT INITIATIVE TO PROTECT GIRLS SPORTS

Colorado voters approved ballot measures increasing penalties for fentanyl-related offenses, restricting transgender athletes from competing in sports designated for the opposite biological sex and prohibiting gender-related surgeries for minors. The measures passed even as Democrats swept into power across the state.

"I don’t believe it would be acceptable to Colorado to have every student athlete to have to go through full-body examinations or other invasions of privacy," Weiser added of the sports-related referendum, according to the Denver Post.

COLORADO MOM WHO SAID DAUGHTER WAS SECRETLY TRANSITIONED HELPS LEAD EFFORT TO BAN BOYS IN GIRLS' SPORTS

Weiser did not respond to a request for comment.

Republicans in suburban Denver criticized the governor-elect, dubbing him "King Phil I" and characterizing his response as "know[ing] better than Colorado voters in a healthy democracy."

"But before the ink on the ballots is even dry, Governor-elect Phil Weiser is already signaling that the vote of the people is merely a ‘suggestion’. With Coloradans approving ballot measures to crack down on fentanyl and protect youth sports and children, Weiser walked up to the podium on Wednesday and essentially declared that the will of the majority needs to pass his personal vibe check first," the Adams County Republican Party said in a statement.

Republicans characterized Weiser’s position as "you voted for it, but I don’t like it…"

"No Kings," the Adams Republicans added, invoking the protest movement that Weiser has supported through participation in "No Kings" protests. The movement's demonstrations have criticized President Donald Trump over what organizers characterize as authoritarian conduct.

The Colorado House Republican caucus echoed the sentiment, adding in a statement: "If the Democrats truly believe there should be ‘No Kings’ in America, it is time they take their own advice."

'NO KINGS' FOOT SOLDIERS IGNORE ORGANIZERS' WARNING, GO ALL IN FOR DEMOCRATS

Meanwhile, in Washington State, Jayapal condemned a similar measure approved by voters.

Initiative 638 prohibits students defined as "biologically male" from competing in girls' K-12 school sports and requires students seeking to participate on girls' teams to provide verification of their biological sex from a health care provider. The measure passed with approximately 56% support in the reliably Democratic state.

Following the election results, multiple local news outlets reported that Jayapal pledged to "take our state back" after voters approved the initiative.

"We're going to start planning for how we overturn these bad initiatives and how we go back to loving everyone with gender inclusivity the way we have for decades," she said, according to several reports.

Jayapal did not respond to a request for comment.

Critics also pointed to Jayapal's past support for "No Kings" protests, accusing her of contradicting her own rhetoric about respecting the will of voters.

One critic highlighted a November 2025 social media post in which Jayapal wrote: "We have democracy for a reason. America doesn’t belong to kings it belongs to the people and we're going to keep it that way."

"Rep. Jayapal, this you?" they asked.

Jayapal also faced previous criticism over her support for the "No Kings" movement after praising remarks by Britain's King Charles III during his visit to the United States.

Washington Democratic Party Chair Shasti Conrad signaled support for a legal challenge, calling the ballot measure "unconstitutional on its face" and indicating the party would "support [for] organizations planning to challenge it in court."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Under Washington's Constitution, lawmakers cannot repeal a voter-approved initiative during its first two years but can amend it with a two-thirds vote in each legislative chamber. After two years, the legislature can amend or repeal the measure with a simple majority.

The controversy leaves Democrats in both states confronting a similar political dilemma: whether to preserve the restrictions voters approved or pursue changes through the legislative and judicial processes available to them.

item.title: Iran-backed terror suspects plotted attack on US troops using vans packed with fuel, DOJ says
item.description: A Justice Department indictment alleges three Iran-backed suspects used fuel-laden vans to target RAF Fairford, a British base housing U.S. troops.
item.content:encoded:
Three suspected Iran-backed terrorists plotted an attack on a British air base housing American troops using vans carrying barrels of fuel, according to a federal indictment unsealed Tuesday by the Justice Department (DOJ).

The eight-count superseding indictment charges Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood Al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali Al-Hassani with terrorism-related offenses tied to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Kata'ib Hizballah. 

Prosecutors say the suspects targeted RAF Fairford in England, where U.S. military aircraft and personnel were stationed.

"Anyone who plans a terrorist plot on a military base housing American service members will be prosecuted by the United States government," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a news release.

IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY

According to the indictment, Al-Hassani directed associates in the United Kingdom to conduct surveillance of RAF Fairford in August, paying one individual to record video of the base's perimeter.

The suspects' associates later obtained three vans and barrels of fuel, researched chemical accelerants and purchased metal objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel, prosecutors said. They also disguised the vans with commercial decals to resemble vehicles belonging to fuel delivery and swimming pool supply businesses.

On Sept. 26, Al-Hassani allegedly directed associates to drive the three vans toward the base. At least two encountered a security roadblock and were unable to proceed. British authorities recovered all three vehicles and arrested their occupants the following morning.

UK POLICE ARREST 'EXPLOSIVE' SUSPECTS NEAR US AIRBASE, KEY TO IRAN WAR

Prosecutors allege Al-Saadi helped coordinate the operation while imprisoned in New York awaiting trial on separate terrorism charges, using telephone calls with family members in Iraq to relay coded messages to his co-conspirators.

During a Sept. 24 call, Al-Saadi allegedly asked about Al-Hassani and instructed relatives to "give him [al-Hassani] money so we can do it."

The alleged plot followed a series of attacks across Europe in March and April that prosecutors say the defendants helped organize on behalf of an Iran-aligned terrorist network. Those attacks targeted synagogues, Jewish organizations, ambulances and an Israeli embassy, and included the stabbing of two Jewish men in London.

Al-Saadi, a dual Iranian Iraqi national, was arrested abroad in May and transferred to U.S. custody. Prosecutors previously accused him of helping direct approximately 18 attacks in Europe and attempting to coordinate an attack on a Manhattan synagogue.

The three defendants face charges, including conspiracy to provide material support to foreign terrorist organizations, financing terrorism and conspiracy to bomb a place of public use. Some charges carry a maximum sentence of life in prison.

item.title: Jamie Raskin calls concerns over spending too much time investigating Trump a media 'narrative'
item.description: Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., dismissed concerns within the party about Democrats in Congress focusing too much on Trump investigations as a media "narrative."
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., called concerns that the incoming Democratic Congress will focus too much time investigating the Trump administration a media "narrative" on Monday.

During an interview on "CNN News Central," host Brianna Keilar noted that Adam Hamilton, a Democrat recently elected to the U.S. Senate, said that he doesn't "want to spend the next two years in trials" against the Trump administration after Democrats regain control of the House and the Senate.

"This is something that we're hearing from a lot of those Democrats who did come in," Keilar said.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Raskin attempted to interrupt Keilar and later dismissed the concern as a "narrative," despite Keilar's reference to comments from an incoming senator.

"That's a narrative the media is trying to drive, but–" Raskin said.

"Well, I'm just quoting him, right? So this is what he said. So is he, are other Democrats going to be disappointed by the amount of time spent on investigations?" Keilar said.

Raskin answered, "No, because we have lots of committees. We have got a brilliant new class of Democratic representatives and senators coming in, and we're going to be able to do it all. We're going to be able to get Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act, health insurance back to the American people. Millions of people have been thrown off of their health plans because of the actions of the Trump administration and their wretched, hideous bill. We're going to be able to restore people's benefits to food in the SNAP program."

CRENSHAW, RASKIN SHOUT EACH OTHER DOWN IN HEATED POST-MIDTERM DEBATE

He added, "We're going to be able to get rid of these ruinous 50% tariffs on Canada and on the rest of the world and begin to bring prices down. If they're all serious in running away from Donald Trump and not wanting to have anything to do with the Iran war anymore, beginning with JD Vance, then they can bring us a plan for how we can extricate from the mess that they have given us in Iran. We can work together on all those things. That will bring gas prices and diesel prices down. We can all work together. Corruption and affordability are really the same issue here with the Trump administration, as usually they have been."

Fox News Digital reached out to Raskin's office and Hamilton's campaign for comment.

Although Raskin initially suggested these concerns were part of a media "narrative," several prominent progressive figures have gone on the record discouraging congressional Democrats from spending the next two years targeting President Donald Trump.

PROGRESSIVES FUME AT HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR SAYING DEMOCRATS WON'T 'GET EVEN' WITH TRUMP

One of them included Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., who made his comments as recently as Sunday on NBC's "Meet the Press."

"Do we want to hold the Trump administration accountable for their corruption, for their illegal, unconstitutional actions? Absolutely," Sanders said.

He stressed that Congress must not focus solely on investigating Trump when issues like high child poverty rates, senior poverty, and economic and privacy threats posed by AI require urgent action.

item.title: Top Dem cries ‘weaponization’ as comments warning young people not to join Trump admin land her in hot water
item.description: Dem Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., cries "weaponization" after Trump ordered the Justice Department to investigate her remarks warning young Republicans about joining his administration.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., is accusing President Donald Trump of escalating a coordinated "weaponization" campaign against her after he ordered the Justice Department to examine remarks she made warning young Republicans they could face "a ton of problems" if they joined his administration.

In a Truth Social post over the weekend, President Trump accused Democrats of political weaponization and singled out Slotkin for "go[ing] after all young people that believe in Republican values" in her October remarks. "By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!" Trump wrote.

In a video response posted Monday, Slotkin defended her remarks, saying she was referring to people who might be asked to violate the law or misuse taxpayer dollars and citing her First Amendment rights.

"A couple weeks ago, I talked about how anyone who is violating the law or misusing taxpayer dollars should be held accountable, and if there's young people who are thinking of joining people who are doing that, they should think twice," Slotkin said. "If you're not violating the law — no problem."

DEMS PIVOT FROM 'AFFORDABILITY' PITCH TO DHS PROBE THREATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

Slotkin said Trump began targeting her after her October remarks, first by "name-checking" her from the Oval Office before he "really ramped up his coordinated play" following Democrats’ midterm election gains. She also pointed to Attorney General Todd Blanche's Sunday television appearances discussing possible investigations. Slotkin said her attorney sent the Justice Department a letter Monday asking, "What are you going to do?"

The Justice Department has not confirmed whether it has opened an investigation into Slotkin. During an interview Sunday on CNN’s "State of the Union," Blanche declined to identify a specific crime when asked whether Democrats’ rhetoric could constitute one, saying, "It depends on what’s said. So, yes, it could be." 

A DOJ spokesperson separately told NBC News that Slotkin’s comments should be evaluated under the facts and law but did not confirm an investigation.

Fox News Digital reached out to the DOJ for comment but did not hear back in time for publication.

OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE AT CENTER OF TRUMP'S ANTI-WEAPONIZATION FUND CASE HIT WITH MISCONDUCT CLAIM

Slotkin's original remarks also prompted a congressional ethics complaint. Michael Bicksel, a University of Chicago student who first publicized her comments, filed the complaint with the Senate Select Committee on Ethics on Oct. 22.

Bicksel argued that Slotkin had proposed using congressional investigations and potential prosecutions to deter young people from joining a Republican administration, asking the committee to determine whether her comments amounted to "improper conduct which may reflect upon the Senate."

Fox News Digital reached out to Slotkin for comment but did not hear back in time for publication.

"It's a coordinated, manufactured response," Slotkin previously said about the backlash to her remarks concerning young Trump supporters. "They want to intimidate you to be quiet."

Slotkin made the remarks Oct. 13 during a University of Chicago discussion about how Democrats could exercise congressional power if they regained control of Congress. Fox News Digital previously reported that Slotkin advocated pursuing "signature cases" against people who enabled Trump rather than focusing exclusively on the president. She also argued that the prospect of legal trouble could deter young Republicans from joining his administration.

The latest dispute follows an earlier Justice Department investigation involving Slotkin and five other Democratic lawmakers who posted a video reminding military personnel and intelligence officials that they were not required to follow unlawful orders. A federal grand jury declined to indict the lawmakers.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

In a letter to Blanche made public Monday, Slotkin's attorney, Preet Bharara, argued that her remarks were protected by the First Amendment and the Constitution's speech or debate clause. Bharara demanded that Blanche publicly confirm the Justice Department would not investigate the senator.

"Just like last time, Senator Slotkin will not be deterred," Bharara wrote. "She will continue to call out corruption by this administration and to exercise her First Amendment rights to speak out against the President’s many abuses of power."

item.title: Shanghai-based tycoon Neville Roy Singham's 'Squad,' Bernie Sanders donations resurface
item.description: FEC records show Neville Roy Singham and CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans have donated a combined $47,000 to Bernie Sanders, Pramila Jayapal and more.
item.content:encoded:
A Shanghai-based tycoon known for pushing Chinese Communist Party talking points, whose activist network is flooding Capitol Hill this week, has directly funded some of the most powerful progressives in Congress, including members of "The Squad."

Federal Election Commission records show that Neville Roy Singham and his wife, CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans, have given more than a combined $47,000 to Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Reps. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Chuy García, D-Ill.

Omar's campaign took $4,200 from the couple from 2019 to 2023, according to FEC records. Singham gave her campaign $2,700 in March 2019, just weeks after she took office, and Evans gave $1,500 in two contributions in November and December 2023. None of it has been refunded.

HOUSE PANEL TO PROBE FOREIGN ‘TROJAN HORSES’ AS SINGHAM SCRUTINY WIDENS

Sanders' campaigns have taken in at least $6,800 from the couple, according to FEC records, most of it for his presidential bids. Singham gave $2,700 to Sanders' 2016 presidential campaign. Evans gave the 2016 campaign $2,800, of which it refunded $200, and at least $252 to his 2020 campaign in 2019. She also gave $1,250 to his Senate campaign committee, Friends of Bernie Sanders, in 2011.

García's campaign took in $1,000 from Singham in August 2018, according to FEC records. He was running for his first term in Congress at the time, after winning the Democratic primary for Illinois' 4th Congressional District, Singham's home city of Chicago. The campaign has not refunded the contribution.

Jayapal has received more from the couple than any other member of Congress, a net $35,700 from 2016 to 2022, according to FEC records. Singham gave her campaign $17,800 and none of it was refunded. Evans gave $22,900, and the campaign refunded $5,000 of it in three payments between 2020 and 2023, leaving $17,900. Most of the couple's money came in 2019 and 2021, including back-to-back maximum contributions from Singham in both years.

Under Federal Election Commission rules, a campaign has 10 days to decide whether to deposit a check or return it.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's, D-NY, campaign returned a $500 contribution from Evans through ActBlue on the day it arrived, Aug. 4, 2018, during her first run for Congress.

Fox News Digital reached out to the offices of Sanders, Jayapal, García and Ocasio-Cortez and Omar's office for comment but did not receive responses.

DHS, WAR DEPT JOIN PROBE INTO SINGHAM NETWORK ALLEGEDLY SOWING DISCORD IN US

After his wedding to Evans in 2017 and the sale of ThoughtWorks, the technology company he founded, Singham directed $285 million to nonprofits and media organizations, according to a Fox News Digital investigation. The People’s Forum received $22.4 million from Singham, while CodePink received $1.33 million. BreakThrough BT Media Inc., which operates BreakThrough News, received $1.098 million, according to tax filings. Singham and his wife, who are both American citizens, now live in Shanghai, China.

Organizations within the Singham network regularly participate in staged anti-ICE, anti-capitalist, anti-data centers and anti-Israel protests – many of which garner national and social media coverage.

FROM AUSTIN TO NEW YORK, PRO-CHINA NETWORK FUELS WEEK OF ANTI-US PROTESTS AS XI MEETS TRUMP

Last month, Evans and CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin embarked on a China propaganda tour across the communist country.

The trip, according to an event promotion link for sign-up on the CodePink website, was 12 days and 11 nights in Shanghai, Chongqing, Zunyi, Loushanguan, Maotai Village and Guiyang with the cost of attendance between $3,000 and $4,000 depending on the total number of participants. The CodePink website said attendees will be "greeted by local Shanghai comrades," and a tour with Benjamin and Code Pink co-founder Jodie Evans is included.

"Explore China’s revolutionary history, while marveling at high-tech infrastructure and modern socialist development," the event description reads. "Highlights include Red Memorials, Historical Re-Enactments and Museums, Socialist Infrastructure, and Rural Revitalization."

Singham’s wife’s California-based nonprofit does not shy away from their mission to rebrand China as an ally – displaying the tagline "China is not our enemy" on their website while actively promoting the "revolutionary history" of the communist country.

HOUSE PANEL SUBPOENAS 3 LEFT-WING GROUPS IN PROBE OF $39M TIED TO MARXIST TYCOON NEVILLE SINGHAM

A slew of federal and congressional investigations have been opened into the Singham network, including a grand jury probe led by the Department of Justice and the Southern District of New York – though Singham has yet to be charged with any crime.

During a House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on South and Central Asia committee hearing in September, Mike Gonzalez, a senior fellow at the Heritage Foundation, cited research saying Singham shares premises with Maku Cultural Communication, a Chinese communications firm that promotes a favorable image of China, and was photographed attending a Chinese Communist Party strategic communications workshop in 2023.

JIM BANKS, GOP LAWMAKERS RALLY BEHIND DOJ PROBE INTO ALLEGED CCP-LINKED FUNDING NETWORK

In a video that Fox News Digital unearthed, Singham stood at the Golden Tulip Hotel in Shanghai during a November 2025 conference and expressed support for "a new world order that is based on multilateralism that President Xi and the CPC [Communist Party of China] and China have proposed."

Earlier this year, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent traveled to New York City for a meeting with Goldman Sachs Chairman and CEO David Solomon, and sources told Fox News Digital that Bessent gave a blunt ultimatum to Solomon.

Bessent told Solomon that Goldman Sachs could face scrutiny for alleged conspiracy in the funneling of the Singham money and urged Solomon to cooperate with federal investigators.

A person familiar with the meeting told Fox News Digital that the discussion wasn't contentious and that Solomon readily agreed to pledge his cooperation with the Justice Department investigation. A spokesperson for the bank said "all distributions from Mr. Singham’s donor-advised fund were made to legal nonprofits, as determined by the IRS. There have been no distributions from the account since August 2023, and it was closed in early 2024."

Fox News Digital reached out to Singham, CodePink and Evans but did not receive responses.

item.title: US warns Americans to avoid famed tourist square after gunman kills 6, injures 15

item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Consulate in Kraków, Poland, has issued a warning to American tourists in the aftermath of a deadly shooting in the historic city's center.

Kraków, Poland's second-largest city, is a historic city and popular tourist destination in the southern region of the country.

AMERICANS WARNED OF VIOLENT PROTESTS AS MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATION FACES SHUTDOWN THREAT

item.title: TV anchor found dead with gunshot wound to head, officials arrest husband
item.description: The broadcaster’s husband claimed he was playing with a firearm when it discharged inside their home, according to a provincial official
item.content:encoded:
The husband of a TV anchor was arrested in Pakistan Sunday after his wife was found dead with a gunshot wound to the head, according to officials.

Rabiya Ahsan, 41, was allegedly killed inside her home in Rawalpindi, according to Punjab Information Minister Azma Zahid Bokhari.

Ahsan worked as a program host for 92 News, where she established herself as a dedicated journalist alongside senior colleagues. She also frequently posted videos about national affairs on social media.

Officials identified her husband as Ahsan Tahir Khan, who claimed he was playing with a firearm in the home when it accidentally discharged, Bokhari said.

POPULAR TV HOST, MEDIA STAR FACES HANGING AFTER CONVICTION IN MAJOR SYNTHETIC DRUG TRAFFICKING CASE

Khan reportedly works as a civil service officer at the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, a government agency that supports citizens living abroad, according to local outlet The Express Tribune, citing police sources.

Police are preparing to pursue a murder case against the suspect, according to the report.

Rawalpindi police also confirmed in a post on X that a woman was killed in a Sunday shooting but did not immediately identify her.

Authorities said officers seized the suspected weapon in connection with the husband's arrest.

Ahsan's body was also transferred to a hospital for a postmortem examination.

HUSBAND CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER REALTOR WIFE FOUND SHOT DEAD INSIDE HOME IN WEALTHY VIRGINIA COUNTY

The news of her death sparked an outpouring of grief across Pakistan's journalism community.

"I am deeply saddened to learn that our ex-colleague anchorperson Rabiya Ahsan is no longer with us," one former colleague said on X.

The Pakistani presidency also expressed sadness over the killing and called for a transparent investigation to ensure those responsible are held accountable.

"The First Lady has expressed deep sadness over the killing of journalist Rabia Ahsan and strongly condemned the violence," the statement read, referring to First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari.

DALLAS PUBLIC DEFENDER’S CHIEF INVESTIGATOR CHARGED WITH WIFE’S MURDER AFTER BLOODY APARTMENT DISCOVERY

She also voiced concern over what she described as a "disturbing pattern" of professional women being targeted and allegedly killed by their husbands in the same metropolitan area.

The first lady recalled the case of Hina Javed, a media executive who was found dead with signs of torture three months ago, according to Dawn. Her husband and a domestic worker were reportedly arrested in connection with her killing.

"Such incidents demand serious attention and accountability. Women must be able to live and work without fear for their lives," the Pakistani presidency said.

item.title: Peltola widens narrow Alaska Senate lead over Sullivan as counting continues
item.description: Mary Peltola's lead over Dan Sullivan grew to 2,517 votes after Monday's ballot drop, but tens of thousands of absentee ballots remain uncounted.
item.content:encoded:
Alaska's still too-close-to-call Senate race is expected to deliver another batch of ballot results Tuesday night after Monday's latest ballot drop expanded Democratic nominee Mary Peltola's lead over incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan to 2,517 first-choice votes.

Still current as of Tuesday midday ET, Peltola stands at 48.6% (106,321 votes) to Sullivan’s 47.5% (103,804) in the ranked-choice voting system that will kick in if neither candidate gets across the 50% threshold.

The controversial race, punctuated by the "Decoy Dan" scheme exposed by The New York Times, has Republican Gerald Heikes at 2.2% (4,865) and independent Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. at 1.7% (3,651 votes). Roughly 75–76% of the expected vote is in, with tens of thousands of early, absentee and questioned ballots still to be counted.

ALASKA SENATE FIGHT HEATS UP AS SULLIVAN MOVES TO BLOCK PELTOLA LAWSUIT OVER REJECTED ABSENTEE BALLOT RECORDS

"After every vote is counted, it is clear that Mary Peltola will be elected Alaska’s next United States Senator," Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce wrote in a statement Tuesday morning after that previous tranche of votes.

"Mary won today’s votes by a margin of 68-30, reflecting major support in key areas from Anchorage and Chevak. This overwhelming margin further strengthens Mary’s path to victory, and Mary is looking forward to continuing her relentless fight to lower costs and put Alaska first in the United States Senate after all votes are counted."

Monday's drop added nearly 5,000 ballots and marked a shift from the razor-thin, 637-vote Peltola edge that had held for days after Election Day.

The incumbent Sullivan and President Donald Trump have both suggested if Peltola does not get to 50% of the vote and ranked-choice voting (RCV) goes to rounds two or three that the Republican would absorb secondary voting strength in the system.

DOJ FACES ‘HEAVY LIFT’ IN ALASKA ELECTION APPEAL AS SEPARATE CRIMINAL PROBE CONTINUES

Under Alaska’s system, if no candidate reaches a majority of first-choice votes, the lowest finisher is eliminated and ballots transfer according to voters’ rankings until one candidate surpasses 50%. Right now, that would be the other Dan Sullivan, which might help Peltola break 50%.

The Official RCV tabulation is scheduled for Nov. 18 after the overseas absentee deadline.

The slow pace matches the timeline Gov. Mike Dunleavy described in an interview Sunday. He called the state’s process "very confusing" and "a slow system," pointing to significant ballot dumps expected Friday, Nov. 13, and Wednesday, Nov. 18.

Dunleavy has also continued an investigation into the "Decoy Dan" candidacy of Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., which some Republicans allege was intended to siphon votes from the incumbent; the governor has said the Division of Elections and the Department of Justice are reviewing related questions.

TRUMP ADMIN PUTS ALLEGED 'DECOY DAN' CONSPIRATORS ON NOTICE IN ALASKA ELECTION SPOILER PROBE

"We're still in the process of bringing in votes and counting votes," Dunleavy said Sunday. "And we are in the midst of investigations as to determine if there was any wrongdoing, especially anything that might resemble perjury or, you know, a misrepresentation of individual's intent on how they wanted their candidacy to be placed on the ballot."

Other statewide races remain fluid on the same ballot count:

MURKOWSKI SNUBS TRUMP-BACKED ALASKA CANDIDATE, ENDORSES DEMOCRAT FOR GOVERNOR

Certification is set for Nov. 25.

Democrats have won control of the Senate for the final two years of President Donald Trump's final term, holding a 54-44 edge with both Alaska and the Mississippi Senate races still too close to call. Democrat Scott Colom leads incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., by about 2,500 votes (49.08%-48.81 %).

If Democrats win both those seats, their party would hold a 56-44 edge in the upper chamber, having gone 9-0 in seats flipped in these midterms.

item.title: No. 2 Duke faces No. 5 Michigan State in State Farm Champions Classic showdown tonight
item.description: College basketball's State Farm Champions Classic pits No. 5 Michigan State against No. 2 Duke tonight at Chicago's United Center in a top-5 clash.
item.content:encoded:
College Basketball has returned to action this season, and while most schools are playing inferior opponents, we do finally have a few ranked matchups. This is pretty much what happens every season. Most schools play lower-level clubs so they can get some easy wins out of the way, figure out their offense, and make adjustments before the Thanksgiving tournaments. Tonight, we have the State Farm Champions Classic, featuring two of the best in the country: Michigan State vs. Duke.

Michigan State comes into the game with a ranking of fifth in the nation, and at least part of that is due to its returning players. Jeremy Fears Jr. has been one of the better guards in college sports and is the catalyst for this team. He makes this team go, and in two games, he has led the team in scoring. It isn't much scoring at just 12 points per game, but either way, he still leads the team. Coen Carr is an athletic forward who thrives on defense and rebounding. Their tenacity will set the tone for Michigan State all season.

The Spartans are 2-0 for the season, but they haven't played anyone of substance. They beat Quinnipiac by 37 points in the season opener, and they beat Toledo by 30 points in the next game. Now they face a true test. The question will be how well some of the newer guys play. Jasiah Jervis led the team in scoring in their last game, and Ethan Taylor is a 7-footer who will cause headaches for everyone. Overall, the team has some depth, consistency, height, and high-motor guys. They should have a chance against anyone in the nation.

Duke is the second-ranked team in the nation, and they are pretty much the same story as every year. In the past two seasons, they had Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel, and Cameron Boozer come in and leave their program. Both seasons ended without a National Championship, but both seasons were successful. The Blue Devils don't have the top-ranked player in the nation this season, but they do have Joaquim Boumtje-Boumtje and Cameron Williams, who are 6'11" or taller.

item.title: Vikings acquire Kirk Cousins from Raiders who turn to Fernando Mendoza as their starting QB
item.description: Kirk Cousins returns to the Minnesota Vikings in a blockbuster trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, sending draft picks for the quarterback.
item.content:encoded:
Kirk Cousins is the new starting quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings after the team agreed with the Las Vegas Raiders to acquire the player that previously played six seasons in the Twin Cities.

So, Kirk Cousins ... once and future Vikings quarterback.

This is a seismic move.

CARTON: DIANNA RUSSINI HAS BOTCHED HER RETURN TO THE SPOTLIGHT - DOWNLOAD NOW

The Vikings are sending a third-round pick to the Raiders in exchange for Cousins with the idea of making him their starter immediately. The club is expected to promote Cousins ahead of both Kyler Murray, who is currently nursing a hamstring injury, and Carson Wentz, who was wildly ineffective in a Monday night loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Cousins, who played for the Vikings from 2018 through 2023 – including two years under current coach Kevin O'Connell – is familiar with much of what the Vikings do on offense, so his arrival in Minneapolis should be as close to seamless as can be expected for any quarterback being traded to a new team in November.

This move at the NFL's trade deadline on Tuesday, also has enormous ramifications for the Raiders beyond the compensation they're getting for the deal.

It means that Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall selection in the 2026 draft, is expected to become the Raiders starter as soon as this week against the Seattle Seahawks.

Mendoza getting his NFL regular-season debut against the defending Super Bowl champions is quite the way to start a career but the rookie has been sitting behind Cousins so far this season and the Raiders obviously felt he was ready to take the next step in his development.

KIRK COUSINS OR FERNANDO MENDOZA? LAS VEGAS RAIDERS SURPRISINGLY DECLINE TO NAME REGULAR-SEASON STARTING QB

So, the Vikings are getting what they believe to be quarterback upgrade in Cousins and the Raiders are getting draft pick compensation and the start of Mendoza's career clock.

But here's a warning to Vikings fans: the Kirk Cousins experience is a roller-coaster ride. There are a lot of ups and a lot of downs.

item.title: Is AI deciding who's dangerous in Michigan prisons?
item.description: Michigan's new prison scoring system claims 30% better violence prediction, but Recidiviz says it doesn't actually use AI to classify inmates.
item.content:encoded:
What if a computer-generated score could influence whether someone lives in a low-security prison dorm or a tightly controlled cell? Michigan is preparing to test new technology that could affect exactly that. 

State officials say the system could improve predictions of future prison violence by approximately 30%. That's a big claim, especially when the safety of correctional officers and incarcerated people could depend on getting those assessments right.

But there's something important missing from early reports about Michigan prison AI. Despite headlines suggesting artificial intelligence will determine how dangerous someone might be, the nonprofit developing the software says AI plays no role in calculating security scores.

Instead, the technology follows predetermined rules, and corrections staff make the final decisions. So, how does the system work? And can Michigan really predict prison violence more accurately without putting too much trust in a computer-generated score?

FEDERAL INMATES MAY SOON GET TABLETS WITH MESSAGING CAPABILITIES AS BUREAU OF PRISONS MAKES MODERNIZATION PUSH

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.

The Michigan Department of Corrections oversees approximately 32,000 incarcerated people statewide. Currently, corrections employees use a manual scoring process to determine the appropriate security level for each person. Those classifications influence where someone lives and how closely they're supervised. They can also affect access to educational programs and job training opportunities. For someone serving a lengthy sentence, a change in security level can make a significant difference in daily life.

Michigan has four general population security levels: I, II, IV and V. Level I generally allows greater freedom of movement, while Level V involves much tighter supervision. People at lower security levels may have access to more vocational training and higher education opportunities. However, Michigan says programs such as Violence Prevention Programming remain available at every general population security level. There is no general population Level III. Now, the state wants a better way to determine which security level fits each person's current behavior and needs.

The Michigan Department of Corrections plans to begin testing the new system on Dec. 1 at selected men's prisons. If the pilot performs well, officials could eventually expand the technology to additional facilities. One significant change involves how often corrections staff can reassess someone's security level. Instead of relying on information collected at scheduled intervals, the new system will allow ongoing reviews using updated prison records. That could help staff recognize changes in behavior sooner.

The software comes from Recidiviz, a nonprofit technology organization that supports criminal justice agencies in 19 states. Its team analyzed 10 years of Michigan prison classification data to help redesign the state's scoring process. Here's how it works. The software examines information already in prison records and calculates a score using factors selected by Michigan corrections experts. Recent disciplinary incidents may carry more weight than incidents from years ago. Meanwhile, someone who maintains good behavior over time may have an opportunity to qualify for a lower security level.

Completing certain rehabilitation programs can also help someone qualify for a less restrictive classification. Additionally, the software can flag a person's record when new information warrants another review. Michigan Department of Corrections Director Heidi E. Washington believes the changes could help improve safety.

"Classifying prisoners at the security level that fits their current behaviors and needs keeps everyone safer," Washington said in the state's announcement. She also expressed optimism that the combination of historical information and research-based scoring could strengthen security throughout Michigan's prison system. The idea sounds promising. But how much confidence should officials place in those computer-generated scores?

GRANDMOTHER SUES AFTER ALLEGED AI FACIAL RECOGNITION ERROR LED TO MONTHS IN JAIL, EXPERTS SOUND ALARM

This is where the story takes an unexpected turn. On Nov. 2, Recidiviz published an explanation titled, Why We Don't Use AI to Classify People in Prisons. The nonprofit confirmed that Michigan's new classification system does not use artificial intelligence to calculate security scores. The system relies on a points-based formula that corrections employees can examine.

You may hear this type of formula called an algorithm. That's simply a set of instructions a computer follows to complete a task. Think of it like a digital scorecard. The computer reviews specific information and adds up the points according to established rules. Give it the same information, and it produces the same score. 

Recidiviz says Michigan corrections experts helped determine which factors belong in the scoring process. Staff can review the calculations and override a score when circumstances require it. For example, someone might have medical needs or personal safety concerns that call for a different housing assignment. Corrections employees can consider that information before making the final decision.

Now, Recidiviz does use AI in other parts of its technology platform. Some tools help corrections employees prepare case notes and organize information from meetings. However, the organization says AI does not determine someone's security level or release. And here's what I find interesting. We're hearing about AI being used in nearly every industry. Yet this particular system relies on a more traditional approach to computer software. 

That clarification is important because people deserve to understand how technology influences decisions affecting someone's daily life. Still, using a rules-based system doesn't guarantee perfect results. Even straightforward software can produce questionable scores when the information behind its calculations contains errors.

This is the number that really caught my attention. In its Oct. 28 announcement, the Michigan Department of Corrections said the redesigned system is expected to improve its ability to predict future violence by approximately 30%. That's a substantial improvement if the technology delivers it. However, the announcement doesn't explain how officials calculated that figure or provide the underlying performance results.

For example, will the system identify more people who might become violent? Could it also incorrectly classify someone as dangerous? And how will officials know whether it's performing better than the current process? Those questions deserve answers because someone's security classification can affect their daily life throughout their sentence. 

There's another issue worth considering. The software depends on prison records. If a disciplinary report contains inaccurate information, that mistake could influence someone's score. Even when the information is correct, a risk assessment cannot predict with certainty what someone will do in the future.

NORTHEASTERN CITY VOTES TO END SHOTSPOTTER CONTRACT FOR GUNFIRE-DETECTION TECH DESIGNED TO FIGHT CRIME

Even if Michigan's new software delivers more accurate security scores, officials still face a challenge that technology cannot solve on its own. What happens when someone needs higher-security housing but there's no appropriate bed available? Byron Osborn, president of the union representing Michigan corrections officers, raised that concern in recent reporting.

According to Osborn, the department faces a shortage of higher-security beds. He argues that the bigger problem involves a lack of appropriate housing for people already classified as higher risk. Consider what happens if the software identifies someone who needs tighter supervision. Corrections staff agree with the assessment, but the prison lacks space in the appropriate security unit.

Now what? The computer may have helped identify a potential safety concern. However, officials still need somewhere appropriate to house that person. Michigan has announced plans to add 870 high-security beds as part of its Safe Prisons Initiative. Some facility conversions are already underway, while larger construction projects will take longer to complete.

More than 400 of those beds will come from two new high-security units at Oaks Correctional Facility and St. Louis Correctional Facility. The state expects those construction projects to take approximately two and a half years. Osborn has warned that corrections officers and incarcerated people need solutions sooner.

Meanwhile, the state has experienced serious violence inside its prisons, including several recent incidents in which incarcerated people were suspected of killing their cellmates. Better classification could help officials recognize potentially dangerous situations sooner. But the department still needs sufficient staffing and appropriate housing to respond. And that raises another question. How much safer can a prison become if officials identify a problem but lack the resources to address it?

I can see why Michigan wants to try something new. Nobody wants to see more violence inside prisons, and if technology can help prevent it, I'm all for giving it a chance. But I was surprised to learn that despite all the talk about AI, this new system actually uses a fairly straightforward scoring process. Corrections staff still make the final decisions, which I think is important when you're dealing with people's safety.

Now, that 30% improvement Michigan is talking about sounds impressive. But I'd really like to know how they arrived at that number. And what happens when the computer gets someone's risk level wrong? Maybe a person has turned their life around, but an old disciplinary record still works against them. That's the kind of situation I'd want someone to take a closer look at before making a decision.

There's also the bigger issue of whether Michigan has enough high-security beds and corrections officers to act on these assessments. You can have the best scoring system in the world, but what good does it do if there's nowhere appropriate to house someone who needs closer supervision? I'll be interested to see what happens when the pilot begins Dec. 1. If it leads to safer prisons and gives people a fairer way to demonstrate they've changed, that would be something worth talking about. But Michigan needs to show us the results.

Would you trust a computer-generated score to help determine how dangerous someone might be, or should decisions affecting someone's safety remain entirely in human hands? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: Jim Jordan becomes new House GOP leader after closed-door vote, defeating Steve Scalise
item.description: Jim Jordan defeated Steve Scalise in a narrow secret ballot to become House GOP minority leader and President Trump's top defender in Congress.
item.content:encoded:
House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, will be President Donald Trump's top defender in Congress next year after winning a closed-door election for minority leader on Tuesday, sources told Fox News Digital.

Jordan defeated Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., currently the House of Representatives' No. 2 leader, in what's believed to be a narrow race. Jordan received 106 votes to Scalise’s 73, sources in the room told Fox News Digital. 

Fox News Digital heard loud, sustained applause from outside in the hallway when Jordan’s win became official.

House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., also handily defeated Republican Study Committee Chairman August Pfluger, R-Texas, for the No. 2 leadership job of minority whip. The final vote count was 103 to 76, per sources.

Sources said House GOP Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain, R-Mich., meanwhile, also survived a challenge and kept her job.

JORDAN EMERGES AS POTENTIAL NEXT GOP LEADER IF DEMS SEIZE HOUSE

Republicans huddled for a candidate forum on Tuesday morning where all GOP lawmakers running for leadership positions were peppered with questions by their colleagues.

Sources inside the room for their Tuesday morning leadership forum said Scalise and Jordan both pitched themselves as the best person to unify the conference, but also signaled they would give a wide berth for lawmakers to "vote their districts," as one person put it.

The question-and-answer session for House Republicans before electing their leader was largely cordial, Fox News Digital was told. Several people inquired about how both prospective leaders would unify the conference after their midterm losses and how they would handle leaks to journalists, Fox News Digital was told.

Jordan himself told Fox News Digital he believed the forum went well but declined to go further, stating he does not divulge details of closed-door meetings.

The voting body consisted of incumbent House Republicans and GOP members-elect who are projected to win their races from last week's midterms. Votes were cast via secret ballot, meaning none of those in the room had to reveal who they chose.

AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI

And the results on Tuesday show the House GOP was hungry for change. Jordan's victory comes fresh off the back of a historic loss for Republicans across both state and federal races.

The magnitude of the losses forced Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., to announce he was stepping aside and not seeking another leadership position for the next two years.

"I personally like Steve, but he's been in leadership since before I was in Congress. And Jim Jordan, while he's a leader in Congress, he hasn't been part of the leadership team. He basically rose through the ranks because he was super effective," Rep. Warren Davidson, R-Ohio, told Fox News Digital.

Rep. Scott Fitzgerald, R-Wis., another Jordan ally, told Fox News Digital the Ohio Republican "understands what we're up against," adding, "His ability to communicate is really kind of unrivaled by anybody else in the House right now."

Jordan has long been among the House GOP's brightest stars, rapidly gaining influence over the last decade as one of Trump's most vocal supporters in Washington.

He will now be the go-to defender as Democrats ready a barrage of investigations targeting Trump's Cabinet, family and business interests.

item.title: Trump closing in on new press secretary as administration officials push for pick who could break the mold

item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: President Donald Trump is closing in on a new press secretary, and administration insiders are advocating for a person who will break the mold

"His name has been brought up to the president by many people," a source close to the president told Fox News Digital Tuesday, referring to conservative commentator Ben Ferguson.

"[Trump's] instincts are to pick a man," the source said. "Which many people have told him that's a good idea."

LEAVITT OPENS UP ON HELPING TRUMP FIND NEW PRESS SECRETARY AFTER ZACHARIA DEBACLE: 'WAS NOT FOR HER'

The source said Trump intends to choose someone to fill the vacant position soon and that he values the role of press secretary in the administration.

A second person familiar with the matter confirmed Trump is planning to pick a man as his next press secretary and said Ferguson is a frontrunner.

The last seven press secretaries, spanning Trump's second term, former President Joe Biden's single term and Trump's first term have all been women. Sean Spicer was the last man to serve in the role. He was Trump's first press secretary from January 2017 to June of that same year. He was replaced by Sarah Huckabee Sanders, who is now governor of Arkansas.

Ferguson is a conservative commentator who hosts the nationally syndicated radio show, "The Ben Ferguson Show." He's also a political commentator on CNN.

But Trump is still weighing his options.

"POTUS is not sold on the idea," the source said of Ferguson. "I think it's safe to say [Ferguson is] pursuing the job, and the president is aware."

Scott Jennings, the conservative CNN contributor who frequently appears on "Newsnight with Abby Phillip" and worked in former President George W. Bush's administration, is also in the running for the job.

"The president keeps going back and forth on Scott Jennings," the source said. "I don't think it will happen."

A few other names have been floated but not emerged as clear picks for the job. This includes White House Communications Director Steven Cheung, Breitbart chief Matthew Boyle and Ari Fleischer, who was White House press secretary during President George W. Bush's first term.

Many woman have also made the short list, but the two sources who spoke with Fox News Digital insist the next person to hold the job will likely be a man.

ALINA HABBA SHUTS DOWN SPECULATION SHE COULD REPLACE KAROLINE LEAVITT AS WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY

Ferguson has support from within the Trump administration, Fox News Digital has learned.

"Ben is one of loudest supporters of President Trump in the 21st century," a senior White House official told Fox News Digital. "While many supporters don’t have the courage to take to the fake news, Ben consistently walks into the lion’s den and faces the media bias head on."

The official said Ferguson runs circles around some people who are currently paid to defend Trump.

JEN PSAKI MOCKS TRUMP’S NEW PRESS SECRETARY, QUESTIONS IF SHE’S A 'POTENTIALLY FAKE LAWYER'

"His resumé and experience are exactly what the administration will need when they face a Congress hell-bent on dismantling our efforts to Make America Great Again," the official continued.

Another Trump administration official echoed that sentiment, claiming, "Ben has always been a skilled and talented commentator."

"He and Scott are screamed at by the radical left everyday as they defend the president to a hostile audience," the official said, adding that the hostility the pair face on cable news is not unlike what they would face standing behind the podium in the White House press briefing room.

"The president needs a tireless, talented communicator at the podium who’ll relay his success for the nation and how he’ll be a bulwark against Democrats’ attempts to dismantle our Republic," the official said.

The White House has been without a press secretary since Oct. 13, when Katie Zacharia left the job at Trump's urging after only a week.

Zacharia's brief tenure was marked by controversy over her claims to be an attorney and a disastrous press conference that lasted only 14 minutes and was widely condemned as a train wreck.

She was selected to replace Karoline Leavitt at the podium after the former press secretary served as a Trump world powerhouse through the 2024 campaign and into his first year-and-a-half back in office.

Leavitt resigned from the post in August after returning from maternity leave, citing a desire to spend more time with her growing family.
